title: a host-bound tooth's verdict is read from the host that can run it
intention: A tooth that reads not-run on the sealer takes its reading from the seal of the host that can run it, for the same tree fingerprint; the verdict stands when every tooth has a green reading from a host able to run it and none reads red.
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 on akiendell (Windows): sail.py verdict 380d524e6e9c was refused, its criterion instrument 'bin/cairn test bin/proofs/test_cairn_runs_from_cmd_with_no_bash.py' exiting 2 with 'cairn test --exec: refused - the instance seal is not confirmed (cannot build the instance seal: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed)'; the same proof's Windows seal was green 3 of 3 and its hollow 0 of 2, committed on main. Outline 9.4.8.1 (a CC line) covers only the bwrap-only tooth, which reads not-run on Windows and is the sealer's; it is silent on the mirror, a tooth only Windows can run (teeth 1 and 3 of that proof read UNRAN on Linux). grep of the repo for CAIRN_VERDICT_SEALER_HOME finds nothing: verdict.py run_instrument runs the instrument locally through the tester's sealed exec, so no far-box path is wired.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: a tooth that reads not-run on the sealing host takes its reading from the seal on file for that tooth on a host able to run it (the validation's own record), accepted only when its tree fingerprint equals the tree under verdict. The verdict stands when every tooth has a green reading from a host able to run it and none reads red; a tooth not-run everywhere refuses, and a red from either host refuses. 9.4.8.1 gains a sibling line for the mirror case.

clauses.claim: 380d524e6e9c's three teeth verdict green from the Windows seal plus the Linux not-run reading
a tooth not-run on every host refuses the verdict
a red reading from either host refuses the verdict
